To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the traD, traM, traY, traD, traZ, and IS3 genes map in the order traD-trai-traz-IS3 and that the traI gene is the structural gene for the DNA helicase required for nicking at ori T.
the traD and traZ genes are located on either side of a 3-kilobase segment of DNA, and the traI and traZ nicking activities are located in different genes.

the traZ nicking activity of the F transfer system may actually be encoded by traI, that the 94 kilodaltons of protein previously assigned to the traZ gene actually arise from the amino terminus and carboxy termini of the 1,200-kilodalton TraI protein, and that the traI gene of F is located 1 kilo base to the right of its previous map position.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a region of the F transfer system that is essential for the initiation of conjugal DNA transport, but its genetic and functional organization is still not fully understood.
the DNA transport and recombination functions of the F transfer apparatus.

the genetic organization of the traDIZ region of the F transfer system and the identification of the TraD, TraI, and TraI* polypeptides, and it has revealed a new translational organization and a possible functional link between DNA helicase and primase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the traI gene encodes a DNA helicase that is essential for nicking at ori T.
the F traDIZ gene region encodes a helicase, a primase-helicases, and a nicking activity.
the traDIZ gene cluster of F is a complex of at least four genes, traD, traZ, and traI and traI*, and that traI* is a translational restart of traI and that TraZ is an unidentified product.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(i) the traDIZ region contains at least one additional tra gene; (ii) the traD and traZ gene products are not known; (iii) the traI gene product is the 94-kD TraI* polypeptide and not the 94-kDa DNA helicase; (iv) TraZ is a function of traDIZ and not traZ; (v) the traD gene is not a member of the traMYDIZ gene cluster;

the distal end region of the F transfer genes has undergone a major reorganization since the original F transfer region was constructed, that the F traDIZ region is now a more complex and more interesting region of the F sex factors than previously thought, and that the F traI gene is an important gene in the DNA helicase family.
the distal end region of traDIZ has been reorganized, the traI gene is a structural gene for DNA Helicase I, and the oriT nicking function is probably a property of TraI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tra genes at the distally located end of the F conjugation operon may be more complex than previously thought.
the traDIZ region is more complex than previously thought and that the traI gene encodes a 94-kilodaton polypeptide (TraI*) that is a translational restart product of the traI gene.

the traI gene, which is the structural gene for helicase I and which has a role in the initiation of DNA transport during conjugation, is located 1 kilo- base to the right of its previously suggested position.
